title: The Golf Driving Range Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The culprit staged two layers of misdirection -- a fake exploded-ball fragment planted at the scene, and a second 'backup' bomb ball planted in Yasui's bag -- to frame a coworker; both are represented as regarding/red-herring evidence rather than implicates, since they are fabrications, not real clues. A second red-herring has_motive_against edge (Okubo, whose product ideas Tachibana took credit for) sits alongside the culprit's real motive and the framed suspect's alleged-but-denied one, fixing v1's near-total label leak. case_type: murder.

persons.name: Eisuke Tachibana
persons.occupation: director of product development, Itsui Electronics

attrs.note: the murder happened on his last day before an overseas promotion to head the New York branch

persons.name: Minoru Yasui
persons.occupation: section manager, product development, Itsui Electronics

attrs.cleared_because: a second, 'backup' bomb ball was planted in his bag to frame him, and his absence during the explosion (fetching Tachibana's coffee, a routine ten-minutes-early errand) was engineered by the real culprit, not a real alibi gap
caught in the blast himself, with injuries across nearly his entire body

attrs.injury_pattern: injuries confined to the outside of his left elbow and leg, consistent with shielding his eyes with his left arm and ducking behind a pillar an instant before the blast -- unlike Okubo's all-over injuries

attrs.hidden_in: the head of Tachibana's own driver
attrs.mechanism: detonates when the club strikes a ball, timed to the victim's own swing rather than to any particular golf ball

attrs.staging_flaw: planted at the scene after the explosion so investigators would assume the bomb had been hidden inside a golf ball rather than the driver itself

objects.name: Backup bomb ball, planted in Yasui's bag

attrs.staging_flaw: planted to look like Yasui kept a spare in case the first 'bomb ball' turned out to be a dud, framing him once the fake exploded-ball fragment was found

attrs.history: a gift from the current CEO 15 years earlier; had a cracked shaft that Minami was asked to get repaired, converting it from a wood head to a carbon shaft
attrs.note: in Minami's sole possession for a full day and night before being returned to Tachibana the morning of the murder

objects.name: Blue-striped golf ball recovered by a far post

attrs.significance: the actual ball Tachibana hit when the bomb went off -- an ordinary blue-striped ball, not the marked red-crossed 'bomb ball', but still faintly smelling of explosives, proving the explosive was in the club, not the ball

clues.desc: The ball recovered by the far post has an ordinary blue stripe, not the red crossed lines marking the supposed 'bomb ball', yet it still smells faintly of explosives -- proving the explosion did not come from a planted ball at all, and that the fragment with a fuse found at the scene was staged afterward.

Minami's injuries were confined to the outside of his left elbow and leg, consistent with instinctively shielding his eyes with his left arm and taking cover behind a pillar an instant before the blast -- behavior that requires knowing almost exactly when the explosion would happen.

Minami specifically warned a bystander (a small child) to stay back because the range was 'dangerous', moments before the explosion -- a warning inconsistent with someone who would be genuinely caught off guard by it.

edges.detail: hides a black-powder bomb inside the driver's head while ostensibly repairing a cracked shaft, during the one full day and night the club was in his sole possession
feigns a stomachache to pass his usual task of collecting Tachibana's golf balls onto Yasui instead
hands Tachibana the sabotaged driver just as Yasui leaves to order the director's usual after-practice coffee

edges.method: black-powder bomb hidden inside the driver's head, detonating when Tachibana swung it

edges.detail: caught in the blast, injured across nearly his entire body
sets down a pre-made ball fragment with a fuse at the scene to suggest the bomb had been in a golf ball
plants a second 'backup' bomb ball in Yasui's bag to frame him

edges.motive_type: professional resentment -- Tachibana never acknowledged his skill or ideas, compounded by contempt for Yasui's sycophancy toward the director
Tachibana took credit for three of his product ideas
alleged old grudge over a girlfriend Tachibana was rumored to have taken from him, which Yasui denies ever happened
